issues.title: YearsBetween fails leap year Feb 29 to Feb 28 equivalence
issues.description: YearsBetween('2012-02-29', '2014-02-28') returned 1 but CQL spec says 2. The code compares (e.month, e.day) = (2,28) < (s.month, s.day) = (2,29) and subtracts 1. But CQL says Feb 28 IS the equivalent day of Feb 29 in non-leap years, so no subtraction should occur.
issues.spec_citation: CQL Appendix H, YearsBetween Scenario 4, Example 4.b
issues.evidence: SQL: SELECT YearsBetween('2012-02-29', '2014-02-28') => 1 (expected 2). Root cause: (e.month, e.day) < (s.month, s.day) comparison does not account for Feb 29 leap year equivalence.
issues.proposed_fix: When comparing day numbers, if the start day is Feb 29 and the end day is Feb 28 in a non-leap year, treat them as equal.

issues.title: YearsBetween negative case uses wrong formula (Scenario 5)
issues.description: YearsBetween('2012-02-20', '2011-03-19') returned -1 but CQL spec says 0. When date1 > date2 and month(date2) > month(date1), CQL Scenario 5 says: years = year(date2) - year(date1) + 1. The code only uses the positive formula and does not handle negative direction.
issues.spec_citation: CQL Appendix H, YearsBetween Scenario 5, Example 5
issues.evidence: SQL: SELECT YearsBetween('2012-02-20', '2011-03-19') => -1 (expected 0). Code computes years = -1, does not adjust because month(date2)=3 > month(date1)=2, but CQL requires adding 1 in this negative scenario.
issues.proposed_fix: Implement separate logic for negative direction per CQL Scenarios 5-8.

issues.title: YearsBetween negative case same month wrong subtraction (Scenario 6)
issues.description: YearsBetween('2013-05-15', '2012-05-10') returned -2 but CQL spec says -1. When date1 > date2 and same month and day2 <= day1, CQL Scenario 6 says: years = year(date2) - year(date1). The code subtracts 1 when (e.day < s.day), which is wrong for negative direction.
issues.spec_citation: CQL Appendix H, YearsBetween Scenario 6, Example 6.b
issues.evidence: SQL: SELECT YearsBetween('2013-05-15', '2012-05-10') => -2 (expected -1). Code: years=-1, then e.day=10 < s.day=15 => years -=1 => -2. Should stay -1.
issues.proposed_fix: For negative direction (date1 > date2), when same month and day2 <= day1, no adjustment needed.

issues.title: YearsBetween negative case same month day2>day1 missing +1 (Scenario 7)
issues.description: YearsBetween('2013-03-20', '2011-03-30') returned -2 but CQL spec says -1. When date1 > date2 and same month and day2 > day1, CQL Scenario 7 says: years = year(date2) - year(date1) + 1. The code does not add 1.
issues.spec_citation: CQL Appendix H, YearsBetween Scenario 7, Example 7
issues.evidence: SQL: SELECT YearsBetween('2013-03-20', '2011-03-30') => -2 (expected -1).
issues.proposed_fix: For negative direction, same month, day2 > day1: add 1 to result.

issues.title: YearsBetween negative case month2<month1 erroneous subtraction (Scenario 8)
issues.description: YearsBetween('2014-08-12', '2013-05-14') returned -2 but CQL spec says -1. When date1 > date2 and month2 < month1, CQL Scenario 8 says: years = year(date2) - year(date1), no adjustment. The code subtracts 1 because (5,14) < (8,12).
issues.spec_citation: CQL Appendix H, YearsBetween Scenario 8, Example 8.a
issues.evidence: SQL: SELECT YearsBetween('2014-08-12', '2013-05-14') => -2 (expected -1).
issues.proposed_fix: For negative direction, when month2 < month1, use year(date2) - year(date1) without adjustment.

issues.title: YearsBetween negative case month2<month1 erroneous subtraction (Scenario 8b)
issues.description: YearsBetween('2015-11-05', '2013-03-29') returned -3 but CQL spec says -2. Same root cause as QA-D12B-005.
issues.spec_citation: CQL Appendix H, YearsBetween Scenario 8, Example 8.b
issues.evidence: SQL: SELECT YearsBetween('2015-11-05', '2013-03-29') => -3 (expected -2).
issues.proposed_fix: Same as QA-D12B-005.

issues.title: MonthsBetween negative case day2<=day1 erroneous subtraction (Scenario 3)
issues.description: MonthsBetween('2013-10-15', '2013-10-02') returned -1 but CQL spec says 0. When date1 > date2 and day2 <= day1, CQL Scenario 3 says: months = (year2-year1)*12 + (month2-month1), no adjustment. The code subtracts 1 because e.day=2 < s.day=15.
issues.spec_citation: CQL Appendix H, MonthsBetween Scenario 3, Example 3.a
issues.evidence: SQL: SELECT MonthsBetween('2013-10-15', '2013-10-02') => -1 (expected 0).
issues.proposed_fix: For negative direction (date1 > date2), when day2 <= day1, no adjustment needed.

issues.title: MonthsBetween negative case day2<=day1 erroneous subtraction (Scenario 3b)

issues.evidence: SQL: SELECT MonthsBetween('2014-05-10', '2013-01-08') => -17 (expected -16).
issues.proposed_fix: Same as QA-D12B-007.

issues.title: MonthsBetween negative case day2>day1 missing +1 (Scenario 4)
issues.description: MonthsBetween('2012-06-11', '2011-08-21') returned -10 but CQL spec says -9. When date1 > date2 and day2 > day1, CQL Scenario 4 says: months = (year2-year1)*12 + (month2-month1) + 1. The code does not add 1.

issues.title: DaysBetween ignores time components - wrong results when datetime strings provided
issues.description: DaysBetween('2012-01-31 12:30:00', '2012-02-01 09:00:00') returned 1 but CQL spec says 0. The function uses _parse_date() which strips time components, but CQL Scenario 1 says when time(date2) < time(date1), subtract 1 from the day difference. Time of day matters for days calculation per CQL spec.
issues.spec_citation: CQL Appendix H, DaysBetween Scenario 1, Example 1
issues.evidence: SQL: SELECT DaysBetween('2012-01-31 12:30:00', '2012-02-01 09:00:00') => 1 (expected 0). Code uses _parse_date which strips time, so only date(2/1) - date(1/31) = 1 day.
issues.proposed_fix: Use _parse_datetime instead of _parse_date to preserve time components, then apply CQL day duration logic considering time of day.

issues.title: DaysBetween ignores time components - negative case wrong (Scenario 3)
issues.description: DaysBetween('2011-12-05 05:00:00', '2011-12-04 08:45:00') returned -1 but CQL spec says 0. Same root cause as QA-D12B-011 - time components stripped.
issues.spec_citation: CQL Appendix H, DaysBetween Scenario 3, Example 3
issues.proposed_fix: Same as QA-D12B-011.

issues.title: HoursBetween uses floor division (//) instead of truncation toward zero
issues.description: HoursBetween('2013-10-10T12:30:00', '2013-10-10T08:40:00') returned -4 but CQL spec says -3. The function uses (e-s).total_seconds() // 3600 which is floor division. CQL requires truncation toward zero: int(-13800/3600) = int(-3.833) = -3, but floor gives -4.
issues.proposed_fix: Replace (e-s).total_seconds() // 3600 with int((e-s).total_seconds() / 3600) for truncation toward zero.

issues.title: HoursBetween floor division: -30 minutes returns -1 instead of 0
issues.description: HoursBetween('2013-10-10T12:00:00', '2013-10-10T11:30:00') returned -1 but CQL spec says 0. -1800 // 3600 = -1 (floor), but int(-1800/3600) = 0 (truncation toward zero). Same root cause as QA-D12B-013.
issues.proposed_fix: Same as QA-D12B-013.

issues.title: DaysBetween ignores timezone offsets - DST case returns wrong result
issues.description: DaysBetween('2017-03-12T00:00:00-05:00', '2017-03-13T00:00:00-04:00') returned 1 but should be 0 (only 23 real hours due to DST transition). Same root cause as QA-D12B-011 - time/timezone stripped by _parse_date.
issues.proposed_fix: Same as QA-D12B-011.

issues.title: HoursBetween floor division with timezone normalization
issues.description: HoursBetween('2011-06-29T15:45:59-05:00', '2011-06-29T13:30:12-04:00') returned -4 but CQL spec says -3. After normalizing to same timezone, the difference is about -3h15m. Floor division gives -4 instead of truncation toward zero -3.
issues.proposed_fix: Same as QA-D12B-013 - use truncation toward zero instead of floor division.

issues.title: HoursBetween: -59m59s returns -1 instead of 0 (truncation toward zero)
issues.description: HoursBetween('2020-01-01T01:00:00', '2020-01-01T00:00:01') returned -1 but should be 0. -3599 // 3600 = -1 (floor), int(-3599/3600) = 0 (truncation toward zero).
issues.proposed_fix: Same as QA-D12B-013.

issues.title: HoursBetween: -1h1s returns -2 instead of -1 (truncation toward zero)
issues.description: HoursBetween('2020-01-01T01:00:01', '2020-01-01T00:00:00') returned -2 but should be -1. -3601 // 3600 = -2 (floor), int(-3601/3600) = -1 (truncation toward zero).
issues.proposed_fix: Same as QA-D12B-013.

issues.title: YearsBetween ignores time components - time of day matters per CQL
issues.description: YearsBetween('2012-03-10 10:20:00', '2013-03-10 09:20:00') returned 1 but CQL spec says 0. The code uses _parse_date which strips time, but CQL explicitly notes that 'time of day is important in this calculation' - if time2 < time1, the year has not fully passed.
issues.spec_citation: CQL Appendix H, YearsBetween Scenario 2, Note after Example 2.a
issues.proposed_fix: Use _parse_datetime to preserve time components in YearsBetween, and compare full (month, day, time) tuples.

issues.title: MinutesBetween uses floor division instead of truncation toward zero
issues.description: MinutesBetween for -59 seconds returns -1 instead of 0. -59 // 60 = -1 (floor), but int(-59/60) = 0 (truncation toward zero). Similarly, -61 seconds returns -2 instead of -1. Same root cause as QA-D12B-013 but for minutes precision.
issues.evidence: MinutesBetween -59s => -1 (expected 0), MinutesBetween -61s => -2 (expected -1). Code uses (e-s).total_seconds() // 60.
issues.proposed_fix: Replace // 60 with int(total_seconds / 60) for truncation toward zero.

issues.title: WeeksBetween uses floor division instead of truncation toward zero
issues.description: WeeksBetween for negative durations returns wrong results. E.g., -8 days: -8 // 7 = -2 (floor), but int(-8/7) = -1 (truncation toward zero). The function uses (e-s).days // 7 which is floor division.
issues.spec_citation: CQL Appendix H, WeeksBetween - Duration = [date2 - date1 (days)] / 7, truncated
issues.proposed_fix: Replace (e-s).days // 7 with int((e-s).days / 7) for truncation toward zero.

issues.title: CalculateAgeIn*At functions ignore NULL as_of parameter and compute age from current date
issues.description: All CalculateAgeIn*At functions (Years, Months, Days, Weeks, Hours, Minutes, Seconds) treat a NULL as_of parameter by falling through to current date/time instead of returning NULL. Per CQL spec, null input should propagate to null output. The _calculate_age function in age.py checks 'if as_of is None' and defaults to now() instead of returning None.
issues.spec_citation: CQL Appendix H, CQL null propagation semantics
issues.evidence: evidence. Verified for all 7 *At variants: YearsAt=35, MonthsAt=409, DaysAt=12459, WeeksAt=1780, HoursAt=299016, MinutesAt=17940960, SecondsAt=1076457600 when as_of=NULL
issues.proposed_fix: In _calculate_age(), return None when as_of is None instead of defaulting to current date/time.

issues.title: Between functions crash when mixing timezone-aware (Z/+offset) and naive datetimes
issues.description: HoursBetween, MinutesBetween, SecondsBetween, and their differenceIn counterparts raise TypeError when one datetime has timezone info (e.g., 'Z' or '+00:00') and the other does not. Python's datetime subtraction rejects mixing offset-aware and offset-naive objects. The _parse_datetime function preserves timezone info via fromisoformat, creating aware datetime objects, while naive strings create naive datetime objects.
issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5 Section 2.4.5 (DateTime comparisons should handle timezone), CQL Appendix H
issues.evidence: TypeError: can't subtract offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes. Affects: HoursBetween('2024-01-15T10:00:00Z', '2024-01-15T12:00:00'), SecondsBetween('2024-01-15T10:30:00Z', '2024-01-15T10:30:01'), etc.
issues.proposed_fix: Normalize all parsed datetimes to offset-aware (UTC) or strip all timezone info before subtraction.

issues.title: Between and differenceIn functions use Python floor division instead of CQL truncation toward zero for negative durations
issues.description: WeeksBetween uses (e-s).days // 7, HoursBetween uses total_seconds() // 3600, MinutesBetween uses total_seconds() // 60. Python's // operator performs floor division (rounds toward negative infinity), but CQL requires truncation toward zero. For example: HoursBetween 1 second before start returns -1 (floor) instead of 0 (truncation). WeeksBetween -13 days returns -2 (floor) instead of -1 (truncation). This affects WeeksBetween, HoursBetween, MinutesBetween, differenceInHours, differenceInMinutes, and differenceInWeeks.
issues.spec_citation: CQL Appendix H: 'The result is truncated toward zero'
issues.evidence: WeeksBetween -13 days = -2 (should be -1). HoursBetween -1.5 hours = -2 (should be -1). MinutesBetween -30.5 min = -31 (should be -30). HoursBetween -1 second = -1 (should be 0). HoursBetween -3599 seconds = -1 (should be 0).
issues.proposed_fix: Replace // (floor division) with int(x / divisor) (truncation toward zero) in WeeksBetween, HoursBetween, MinutesBetween, differenceInHours, differenceInMinutes, differenceInWeeks.

issues.title: Multi-component Observation valueQuantity extraction works correctly

All component navigation paths work as expected.
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4 Observation - component.valueQuantity vs valueQuantity
issues.evidence: Observation.valueQuantity on BP = [] (correct, no top-level VQ). Observation.component.valueQuantity = [JSON{120,mmHg}, JSON{80,mmHg}] (correct). component.where(code.coding.code = '8480-6').valueQuantity.value = ['120'] (correct systolic). component.where(code.coding.code = '8462-4').valueQuantity.value = ['80'] (correct diastolic). Observation.value on BP = [] (correct, no top-level value). Observation.value on simple lab with valueQuantity resolves correctly. NOTE: Values are returned as strings (e.g., '120' not 120) but arithmetic operations still work.
issues.resolution_notes: Component-based Observation navigation works correctly. String type coercion noted but functional.

issues.title: Reference range extraction with multiple ranges works correctly
issues.description: Observations with multiple reference ranges (normal, hyperthyroid, hypothyroid) correctly return all values via Observation.referenceRange.low.value/high.value. Filtering by type.coding.code = 'normal' correctly returns only the normal range values. Text-based filtering with where(text = 'Hypothyroid') also works correctly.
issues.evidence: referenceRange.low.value returned 3 values: ['0.400000', '0.000000', '4.000000'] (correct). referenceRange.high.value returned 3 values: ['4.000000', '0.400000', '10.000000'] (correct). where(type.coding.code = 'normal').low.value = ['0.400000'] (correct). where(type.coding.code = 'normal').high.value = ['4.000000'] (correct). where(text = 'Hypothyroid').high.value = ['10.000000'] (correct). Glucose obs normal range low = ['70'] (correct).

issues.title: where() fails on CodeableConcept fields with multiple coding elements
issues.description: When a CodeableConcept's 'coding' array contains multiple Coding elements, FHIRPath where(coding.code = 'X') returns empty [] regardless of whether 'X' is present. This affects ALL CodeableConcept fields: Observation.interpretation, Observation.category, Observation.referenceRange.type, Observation.code, etc. When the coding array has exactly ONE element, where() works correctly. When it has 2+ elements, where() always returns empty. Workaround: where(coding.exists(code = 'X')) works correctly regardless of array size.
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4 CodeableConcept.coding (array of Coding) / FHIRPath where() function
issues.evidence: Test with interpretation = [{coding: [{code: 'H'}, {code: 'HH'}]}, {coding: [{code: 'A'}]}]: interpretation.coding.code = ['H', 'HH', 'A'] (flattening works). interpretation.where(coding.code = 'H') = [] (BUG: should match first CC). interpretation.where(coding.code = 'HH') = [] (BUG: should match first CC). interpretation.where(coding.code = 'A') = ['A'] (correct: only 1 coding in this CC). interpretation.where(coding.exists(code = 'HH')) = ['H', 'HH'] (workaround works). Same pattern confirmed with category, referenceRange.type, and code fields. Category with single coding: where(coding.code = 'X') works. Category with multiple coding: where(coding.code = 'X') returns [].
issues.proposed_fix: The where() function's equality check on a nested array property needs to check if ANY element of the array matches, not just the first or some incorrect logic. When evaluating 'coding.code = X' inside where(), the implementation should iterate over all coding elements and return true if any match.

issues.title: where() on root singleton returns empty
issues.description: Applying where() directly at the root of a FHIRPath expression on a single resource (e.g., 'where(status = "final").valueQuantity.value') returns empty. This is because where() requires a collection input, and the root resource is a singleton. The workaround is to use 'Observation.where(status = "final").id' which works correctly. Per FHIRPath spec, where() should theoretically handle singleton collections (a single-item collection), but the common use pattern is to filter collections like component, category, etc.
issues.evidence: where(status = 'final') returns []. Observation.where(status = 'final').id returns ['obs-qty-1']. component.where(code.coding.code = '8480-6') returns correct results.
issues.resolution_notes: Root-level where() is an uncommon pattern in FHIRPath. Typical patterns filter nested collections (component, category, etc.) or use Observation.where() with type qualifier.

issues.evidence: where(category.coding.code = 'laboratory').valueQuantity.value returns []. category.where(coding.code = 'laboratory').coding.code returns ['laboratory'] correctly.
issues.resolution_notes: Use category.where() to filter category elements directly, not where() on root.

issues.title: CQL parser rejects FHIRPath where() function in dot-chain expressions
issues.description: When using FHIRPath where() function within CQL definitions in dot-chain notation (e.g., AllConditions.code.coding.where(code = 'E11.9').exists()), the CQL parser fails with: "Expected identifier, got WHERE 'where'". This prevents using FHIRPath filtering within CQL definition expressions. The CQL-native where clause (e.g., [Condition] C where C.code.coding.code contains 'E11.9') works as a workaround.
issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5: FHIRPath expressions within CQL definitions should support all FHIRPath functions including where()
issues.evidence: CQL: define DiabetesCheck: AllConditions.code.coding.where(code = 'E11.9').exists() -> Error: Line 4, Column 49: Expected identifier, got WHERE 'where'. Workaround using CQL where works: [Condition] C where C.code.coding.code contains 'E11.9' returns correct results.
issues.proposed_fix: Extend the CQL parser to recognize where() as a valid FHIRPath function call within dot-chain expressions, distinct from the CQL where keyword.

issues.title: CQL count() on retrieve result causes SQL type mismatch
issues.description: When applying count() to a CQL retrieve result (e.g., AllConditions.count() where AllConditions is [Condition]), the SQL translation generates array_length(JSON) which fails with: "Binder Error: No function matches the given name and argument types 'array_length(JSON)'. You might need to add explicit type casts." The Count([Condition]) aggregate function works correctly as a workaround.
issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5: FHIRPath count() should be translatable to SQL for collection-typed expressions
issues.evidence: CQL: define CondCount: AllConditions.count() -> Binder Error: No function matches the given name and argument types array_length(JSON). Workaround Count([Condition]) returns correct counts.
issues.proposed_fix: Fix SQL translation of count() to properly handle JSON-typed columns by adding appropriate JSON array length handling or type casting.

issues.title: CQL first() on retrieve result returns malformed JSON [{]
issues.description: When applying first() to a CQL retrieve result (e.g., AllConditions.first() where AllConditions is [Condition]), the result is malformed: "[{]" instead of the expected JSON representation of the first Condition resource.
issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5: FHIRPath first() should return the first element of the collection
issues.evidence: CQL: define FirstCond: AllConditions.first() -> Returns [{] instead of the Condition resource JSON. AllConditions itself returns [Condition/diabetes-1].
issues.proposed_fix: Fix the SQL translation of first() to properly extract the first element from a JSON array column and return the complete JSON object.

issues.title: Boolean values returned as strings instead of native boolean type
issues.description: FHIRPath extraction of boolean values (MedicationRequest.substitution.allowedBoolean, MedicationRequest.doNotPerform) returns Python strings 'true'/'false' instead of boolean True/False. This also affects all other primitive types: integers are returned as strings ('3' instead of 3), decimals as strings ('30.5' instead of 30.5). The FHIRPath spec defines boolean, integer, and decimal as distinct types, and returning them all as strings makes type-dependent operations unreliable.
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4 MedicationRequest.substitution.allowedBoolean: http://hl7.org/fhir/medicationrequest-definitions.html#MedicationRequest.substitution. FHIRPath spec Section 3 (Types): boolean, integer, decimal, string, date, dateTime, time, quantity are distinct primitive types.
issues.evidence: allowedBoolean=True -> ['true'] (str), allowedBoolean=False -> ['false'] (str), doNotPerform=True -> ['true'] (str), numberOfRepeatsAllowed=3 -> ['3'] (str), quantity.value=30.5 -> ['30.5'] (str). All primitive values are stringified regardless of FHIR type.
issues.proposed_fix: Preserve native FHIR types in the FHIRPath engine output: return Python bool for FHIR boolean, Python int for FHIR integer, Python float for FHIR decimal.

issues.title: dateTime vs date literal comparison returns empty when on same calendar date
issues.description: When a FHIR dateTime value that includes a time component (e.g., '2024-01-15T10:30:00Z') is compared using ANY comparison operator (>, >=, <, <=, =) against a FHIRPath date-only literal (e.g., @2024-01-15), the result is an empty collection [] instead of the expected boolean. This affects all medication resource types with dateTime fields. Per FHIRPath spec, a date literal should be comparable to a dateTime by treating the date as the start of the day (T00:00:00Z). Workaround: using dateTime literals (e.g., @2024-01-15T00:00:00Z) works correctly. This bug was found in MedicationDispense.whenPrepared >= @2024-01-15 returning empty [], MedicationDispense.whenPrepared = @2024-01-15 returning empty [], and MedicationStatement.effectivePeriod.start >= @2024-01-01 returning empty [].
issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath spec 2.3.3: Comparing dateTime to date types should be supported. FHIR R4 MedicationDispense.whenPrepared (dateTime), MedicationDispense.whenHandedOver (dateTime), MedicationStatement.effectiveDateTime (dateTime).
issues.evidence:
Comprehensive test results:
- whenPrepared='2024-01-15T10:30:00Z' >= @2024-01-15 -> [] (expected ['true'])
- whenPrepared='2024-01-15T10:30:00Z' >= @2024-01-15T00:00:00Z -> ['true'] (correct)
- whenPrepared='2024-01-15T10:30:00Z' > @2024-01-15 -> [] (expected ['true'])
- whenPrepared='2024-01-15T10:30:00Z' < @2024-01-15 -> [] (expected ['false'])
- whenPrepared='2024-01-15T10:30:00Z' = @2024-01-15 -> [] (expected ['false'])
- effectivePeriod.start='2024-01-01T00:00:00Z' >= @2024-01-01 -> [] (expected ['true'])
- authoredOn='2024-01-15' (date-only) = @2024-01-15 -> ['true'] (correct, no time component)
- where(whenPrepared >= @2024-01-15).id -> [] (empty, should return id)
- where(whenPrepared >= @2024-01-15T00:00:00Z).id -> ['md2'] (correct with workaround)
issues.proposed_fix: Implement FHIRPath type coercion for dateTime vs date comparisons: when comparing a dateTime to a date literal, promote the date to dateTime by appending T00:00:00Z (start of day in UTC) before comparison. This matches the FHIRPath specification for cross-type comparisons.

issues.title: dateTime equality comparison with date literal also returns empty (same root cause as D15A-010)
issues.description: As a corollary to D15A-010, the equality operator (=) between dateTime values and date-only literals also returns empty. For example, '2024-01-15T10:30:00Z' = @2024-01-15 returns []. Per FHIRPath semantics, comparing a dateTime to a date should either return false (if different types are not equal) or should promote the date. Either way, [] is incorrect.
issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath spec 2.3.3: Type coercion in comparisons.
issues.evidence: '2024-01-15T10:30:00Z' = @2024-01-15 -> [], '2024-01-15T10:30:00Z' = @2024-01-15T10:30:00Z -> ['true']. All equality comparisons between dateTime values and date literals return empty.
issues.proposed_fix: Same fix as D15A-010: implement type promotion for dateTime/date comparisons.

issues.title: Boolean FHIRPath results returned as string literals 'true'/'false'
issues.description: FHIRPath queries on boolean fields (active, deceasedBoolean, communication.preferred) return string values 'true'/'false' rather than native Python booleans. This is a common behavior in FHIRPath implementations but consumers should be aware.
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4 Section 2.1.0 - FHIRPath evaluation returns typed collections
issues.evidence: active=True returned as: ['true']; deceasedBoolean=False returned as: ['false']; communication.preferred=True returned as: ['true']
issues.proposed_fix: Document that boolean results are string-typed in fhirpath() output

issues.title: Integer FHIRPath results returned as string representations
issues.description: FHIRPath queries on integer fields (multipleBirthInteger) return string values like '3' rather than native Python integers. Type fidelity is lost in the fhirpath() UDF output.
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4 Section 2.1.0 - FHIRPath evaluation returns typed collections
issues.evidence: multipleBirthInteger=3 returned as: ['3']
issues.proposed_fix: Document that integer results are string-typed in fhirpath() output

issues.title: ViewDefinition forEach generates absolute FHIRPath instead of relative paths
issues.description: When generating SQL for ViewDefinition with forEach on Patient demographic arrays (name, address, telecom, identifier, communication), the column FHIRPath expressions use absolute paths (e.g., 'name.family', 'address.city', 'telecom.system') instead of relative paths ('family', 'city', 'system'). The forEach unnests the array into individual JSON elements, so subsequent column paths must be relative to that element. Since the unnested element is a single JSON object like {"family":"Smith","given":["John"]}, applying fhirpath_text(elem, 'name.family') finds no match because 'name' does not exist within a single name object. The correct path should be 'family'. This affects ALL forEach usage across Patient demographics including name, address, telecom, identifier, and communication. Nested forEach (e.g., forEach=name with inner forEach=given) has the same issue.
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4 ViewDefinition spec: 'When a select has a forEach, the FHIRPath expressions in column definitions within that select are evaluated in the context of each individual element.' Per HL7 FHIR ViewDefinition: column paths inside forEach should be relative to the iterated element.
issues.evidence: Generated SQL for forEach=name: 'fhirpath_text(name_elem_0, 'name.family')' returns NULL. Fixed with relative path: 'fhirpath_text(name_elem_0, 'family')' returns 'Smith'. Confirmed for all forEach variants: name, address, telecom, identifier, communication - all return None for all columns.
issues.proposed_fix: In generate_view_sql, when processing columns inside a forEach block, strip the forEach element name prefix from column paths. For example, if forEach='name' and column path is 'name.family', the generated SQL should use 'family' as the path argument. The transformation should be: for each column path in a forEach context, remove the forEach element name and the following '.' from the beginning of the path.

issues.title: Patient with empty string id not queryable after load
issues.description: When a Patient resource is loaded with id='' (empty string), the resource is stored but cannot be found via SELECT ... WHERE id = ''. The loader stores the resource but the empty-string id prevents retrieval.
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4: id is required 1..1 on all resources. Empty string is not a valid FHIR id.
issues.evidence: Load succeeds, but SELECT resource FROM resources WHERE id = '' returns no rows. The resource exists in the table but with id='' which may not match the WHERE clause correctly.
issues.proposed_fix: Either reject resources with empty-string id during load (with clear error message), or auto-generate a UUID as fallback.

issues.title: Patient with null id not queryable after load
issues.description: When a Patient resource is loaded with id=null, the resource is stored with id=NULL but cannot be found via WHERE id = 'null' or WHERE id IS NULL standard SQL patterns.
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4: id is required 1..1 on all resources.
issues.evidence: Resource is stored but SQL SELECT with any id lookup fails to find it.
issues.proposed_fix: Reject resources with null id, or auto-generate UUID.

issues.title: Patient without id field not queryable after load
issues.description: When a Patient resource is loaded without an id field at all, the resource is stored with id=NULL and cannot be retrieved.
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4: id is required 1..1 on all resources.
issues.evidence: Resource loads successfully but cannot be found by id query.
issues.proposed_fix: Auto-generate UUID for resources without id, or reject with clear error.

issues.title: Completely empty Patient (no fields except resourceType) not queryable

issues.evidence: Resource stored with NULL id, cannot be retrieved.
issues.proposed_fix: Reject empty Patient resources or auto-generate id.

issues.title: FHIRDataLoader accepts non-Patient resourceType without validation
issues.description: FHIRDataLoader.load_resource() accepts resources with resourceType other than 'Patient' (e.g., 'Observation'). It does not validate that the resource type matches expected type.
issues.spec_citation: FHIR data loaders may accept any resource type for generic loading, but should document this behavior.
issues.evidence: Observation resource was loaded via FHIRDataLoader without error.
issues.proposed_fix: Document that FHIRDataLoader is resource-type agnostic, or add optional type filtering.

issues.title: Lowercase 'patient' resourceType accepted without normalization
issues.description: Resource with resourceType='patient' (lowercase p) is accepted and stored as-is, without normalizing to 'Patient'.
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4 specifies resourceType as 'Patient' with capital P.
issues.evidence: resourceType stored as 'patient' instead of 'Patient'.
issues.proposed_fix: Normalize resourceType casing or validate against allowed values.

issues.title: deceasedDateTime not interpreted as deceased=true for Patient.deceased
issues.description: When a Patient has deceasedDateTime (instead of deceasedBoolean), querying Patient.deceased via fhirpath_bool returns None instead of True. Per FHIR spec, the presence of deceasedDateTime means the patient IS deceased.
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4 Patient.deceased[x]: Choice of boolean or dateTime. When deceasedDateTime is present, the patient is deceased.
issues.evidence: Patient with deceasedDateTime='2024-06-15T10:30:00Z': fhirpath_bool('Patient.deceased') returns None. Expected: True. Note: Patient.deceased.exists() correctly returns True.
issues.proposed_fix: fhirpath_bool should recognize deceasedDateTime as meaning deceased=true. When the polymorphic deceased[x] field is a dateTime, it should be treated as boolean true.

issues.title: fhirpath_date accepts non-date string 'true' and pads it to 'true-01-01'
issues.description: When birthDate is set to the string 'true', fhirpath_date pads it to 'true-01-01' instead of returning NULL or an error. The warning 'Date has only year precision' is logged.
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4 date type requires YYYY, YYYY-MM, or YYYY-MM-DD format.
issues.evidence: birthDate='true' -> fhirpath_date returns 'true-01-01' with warning. Invalid dates should return NULL.
issues.proposed_fix: Validate date format before parsing. Return NULL for invalid date strings.

issues.title: FHIRPath .where() with empty result set causes crash in fhirpath_text and fhirpath_json
issues.description: When .where() filters to an empty collection and then a subsequent path step is applied (e.g., Patient.name.where(use='official').family when the name has no 'use' field), both fhirpath_text and fhirpath_json crash with an exception. This happens when: (1) the where clause matches no elements, (2) the source collection is empty, (3) accessing sub-path on empty where result. This is a critical issue as it prevents safe use of where() with potentially empty results.
issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath R4: .where() returns an empty collection when no elements match. Subsequent navigation on empty collection should return empty collection, not crash.
issues.evidence:
Multiple crash scenarios:
- Patient.name.where(use='official').family -> crash (name has no use field)
- Patient.identifier.where(system='x').value -> crash (no identifiers at all)
- Patient.telecom.where(system='phone').value -> crash (no telecom at all)
Even when the where clause matches (family='Smith'), accessing sub-properties crashes: Patient.name.where(family='Smith').family -> crash
Error: 'FHIRPathError' or similar exception on empty collection navigation.
issues.proposed_fix: When .where() returns an empty collection, subsequent path navigation should also return an empty collection. fhirpath_text should return None, fhirpath_json should return None. The engine must handle empty collections gracefully throughout the path evaluation chain.

issues.title: FHIRPath .where().exists() crashes when where returns empty set
issues.description: When chaining .where() followed by .exists(), if the where clause returns an empty collection, fhirpath_bool crashes. This includes both cases where the where clause matches nothing AND cases where it matches something but then .exists() is called.
issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath R4: .exists() on empty collection returns false. Should not crash.
issues.evidence:
Patient.name.where(family='Smith').exists() -> crash
Patient.name.where(family='NotFound').exists() -> crash
Patient.identifier.where(system='x').exists() -> crash
issues.proposed_fix: Handle empty collection from .where() before passing to .exists(). Empty.exists() should return False.

issues.title: FHIRPath .contains() function causes crash
issues.description: fhirpath_bool with expression 'Patient.name.family.contains("Smith")' crashes. The .contains() function is a standard FHIRPath function that should check if a collection contains a value.
issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath R4: contains(substring) is a string function. For collections, use includes().
issues.evidence: fhirpath_bool('Patient.name.family.contains("Smith")') crashes with exception.
issues.proposed_fix: Implement .contains() for string values. Note: FHIRPath uses .contains() for substring check on strings, not collection containment.

issues.title: Patient without id gets null id in storage
issues.description: When a Patient resource is loaded without an id field, it is stored with id=NULL. The resource exists in the table but cannot be easily queried.
issues.evidence: Stored id is NULL for Patient without id field.
issues.proposed_fix: Auto-generate UUID for resources without id.

issues.title: FHIRPath is() type specifier is case-sensitive (String vs string)
issues.description: FHIRPath .is(String) returns False, while .is(string) returns True. The type name must be lowercase. This differs from many FHIRPath implementations where both cases work.
issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath spec: type names in is() are case-sensitive and use lowercase by convention (string, boolean, integer, decimal, date, datetime, time, quantity).
issues.evidence: Patient.gender.is(String) -> False; Patient.gender.is(string) -> True
issues.proposed_fix: Document the case-sensitivity requirement or normalize type names to lowercase.

issues.title: fhirpath_is_valid only validates syntax, not semantic path validity
issues.description: fhirpath_is_valid('Patient.nonexistent') returns True even though 'nonexistent' is not a valid FHIR element. The function only checks if the expression is syntactically valid FHIRPath, not whether the path resolves to an actual element.
issues.spec_citation: Depends on intended behavior - syntax-only validation may be acceptable.
issues.evidence: fhirpath_is_valid('Patient.nonexistent') = True
issues.proposed_fix: Document that fhirpath_is_valid only checks syntax. Consider adding fhirpath_path_exists() for semantic validation.

issues.title: Null fields preserved in stored JSON (correction from Phase 2)
issues.description: Earlier Phase 2 testing appeared to show null fields being stripped, but Phase 4 deep investigation confirmed that null fields ARE preserved in stored JSON. name: null and gender: null are correctly stored as null in the resource JSON. The exists() function correctly returns False for null fields. This is correct behavior.
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4: null values are valid and distinct from absent fields.
issues.evidence: Stored JSON contains 'name': null, 'gender': null when explicitly set to null. exists() correctly returns False.
issues.proposed_fix: No fix needed - behavior is correct.

issues.title: JSON roundtrip fidelity is excellent for standard data

No data corruption detected for well-formed JSON values.
issues.evidence: Tested: Chinese, Arabic, emoji, control chars, HTML tags, 15K char strings, international addresses, special characters in identifiers. All preserved exactly.
issues.proposed_fix: No fix needed.

issues.domain: Domain 17A: DQM Audit / Data Quality (Hypothesis Attacker)
issues.title: ViewDefinition where parser splits FHIRPath expression into individual characters
issues.description: The ViewDefinition parser treats the 'where' FHIRPath expression string as an iterable and splits it into individual character paths. For example, where="gender = 'male'" is parsed as [{'path': 'g'}, {'path': 'e'}, {'path': 'n'}, ...]. This causes the SQL generator to emit fhirpath_bool(resource, 'g') AND fhirpath_bool(resource, 'e') for each character, which is completely wrong. The where clause is effectively non-functional.
issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR v2 spec: where is a FHIRPath expression that evaluates to boolean
issues.evidence:
Input: where="gender = 'male'"
Parsed: [{'path': 'g'}, {'path': 'e'}, {'path': 'n'}, {'path': 'd'}, {'path': 'e'}, {'path': 'r'}, {'path': ' '}, {'path': '='}, {'path': ' '}, {'path': "'"}, {'path': 'm'}, {'path': 'a'}, {'path': 'l'}, {'path': 'e'}, {'path': "'"}]
Generated SQL includes: AND fhirpath_bool(t.resource, 'g') = true for each character
issues.proposed_fix: Fix the where clause parser to treat the string as a single FHIRPath expression, not as an iterable of characters. The parser should create a single where condition, not a list of character-by-character paths.

issues.domain: Domain 17A: DQM Audit / Data Quality (Hypothesis Attacker)
issues.title: CQL Patient.active.value returns None for primitive boolean fields
issues.description: In FHIR R4 JSON, primitive fields like 'active' are serialized as plain booleans (true/false), not as objects with a .value property. CQL's Patient.active.value pattern expects the FHIR representation to have a nested value property, but JSON serialization uses primitives. This causes active.value to return None instead of the actual value.
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4 JSON serialization: primitives are JSON primitives, not objects with value property
issues.evidence: fhirpath_bool(resource, 'active.value') returns None for Patient with active=true
issues.proposed_fix: Consider that in FHIR R4 JSON, 'active' is directly a boolean, not {'value': true}. The CQL .value accessor for primitives may need special handling.

issues.domain: Domain 17A: DQM Audit / Data Quality (Hypothesis Attacker)
issues.title: AgeInYears() standalone always fails with type mismatch - YearsBetween(VARCHAR, DATE)
issues.description: AgeInYears() function fails even when used standalone (not combined with any other criteria). The _patient_demographics CTE stores birth_date as VARCHAR (via CAST(fhirpath_date(...) AS VARCHAR)), but the current date reference in the YearsBetween call is generated as a DATE type. This causes a Binder Error because YearsBetween only has a (VARCHAR, VARCHAR) signature. This is a critical regression as AgeInYears() is a fundamental CQL function used in virtually every clinical quality measure.
issues.spec_citation: CQL spec: AgeInYears() returns the age in years of the patient as of today
issues.evidence: Binder Error: No function matches the given name and argument types YearsBetween(VARCHAR, DATE). You might need to add explicit type casts. Candidate functions: YearsBetween(VARCHAR, VARCHAR) -> BIGINT. SQL: SELECT _pt.patient_id, YearsBetween((SELECT _pd.birth_date FROM _patient_demographics _pd WHERE _pd.patient_id = _pt.patient_id), current_date) AS Age
issues.proposed_fix: Cast the second argument to YearsBetween to VARCHAR: YearsBetween(birth_date, CAST(current_date AS VARCHAR))

QA-D17A-007: in_valueset UDF not registered
issues.description: The in_valueset UDF is not registered when using fhir4ds.register(con) without a valueset_cache parameter. The core.register_cql() function in core.py only registers in_valueset via _register_valueset_cache() when a valueset_cache is explicitly provided. issues.proposed_fix: Register a placeholder in_valueset UDF in core.register_cql() that raises a clear error message when no valueset_cache is provided, similar to the old extension.py placeholder. Alternatively, always create an empty valueset cache and register the UDF with it.

issues.title: ViewDefinition where clause iterated character-by-character when passed as string
issues.description: When the ViewDefinition 'where' field is passed as a string (e.g., 'active') instead of the expected list-of-dicts format ([{'path': 'active'}]), the generator silently accepts it and iterates the string character by character, generating separate fhirpath_bool calls for each character. For example, where='active' generates: AND fhirpath_bool(resource, 'a') = true AND fhirpath_bool(resource, 'c') = true ... etc. This means ALL where clauses passed as strings produce incorrect SQL that matches nothing. The system should either validate the where field format or gracefully convert strings to the correct format.
issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR v2 spec: where field must be array of objects with 'path' key
issues.evidence: where='active' produces SQL: AND fhirpath_bool(t.resource, 'a') = true AND fhirpath_bool(t.resource, 'c') = true AND fhirpath_bool(t.resource, 't') = true AND fhirpath_bool(t.resource, 'i') = true AND fhirpath_bool(t.resource, 'v') = true AND fhirpath_bool(t.resource, 'e') = true. Correct format where=[{'path': 'active'}] produces: AND fhirpath_bool(t.resource, 'active') = true
issues.proposed_fix: Validate where field format: must be list of dicts with 'path' key. Raise clear error if string is passed.

issues.title: evaluate_measure output_columns parameter treats type values as SQL table names
issues.description: When evaluate_measure is called with output_columns={'InInitialPopulation': 'boolean'}, the generated SQL references 'boolean' as a table name instead of using it as a type annotation. Error: CatalogException: Catalog Error: Table with name boolean does not exist! This applies to all type values: 'boolean', 'integer', 'string', etc.
issues.spec_citation: evaluate_measure API: output_columns maps definition names to SQL types
issues.evidence: output_columns={'IsActive': 'boolean'} produces SQL: LEFT JOIN "boolean" ON _pt.patient_id = "boolean".patient_id. Error: Catalog Error: Table with name boolean does not exist!
issues.proposed_fix: output_columns values should be used as type annotations (CAST targets), not as table references in JOIN clauses

issues.title: register_fhirpath() and register_cql() always return False despite successful registration
issues.description: Both register_fhirpath(con) and register_cql(con) return False (bool type), but the UDFs are actually registered and functional. This is misleading - consumers checking the return value would incorrectly assume registration failed.
issues.spec_citation: register() returns dict; register_fhirpath() and register_cql() return bool per API signature
issues.evidence: register_fhirpath(con) returns False, but fhirpath() UDF is available. register_cql(con) returns False, but evaluate_measure() works. register(con) returns a dict (correct behavior).
issues.proposed_fix: Return True on successful registration, or return the dict of registered UDFs

issues.title: ViewDefinition forEach parent-level columns resolve against child element instead of parent resource
issues.description: When a ViewDefinition has a forEach on a select block, columns defined at the forEach level (like 'id' or 'status') are resolved against the unnested child element instead of the parent resource. For example, with forEach='component' on Observation, the 'id' column resolves against the component element (which has no 'id'), returning NULL. Expected: 'id' should resolve against the parent Observation resource. This is a variant/amplification of the known 'forEach uses absolute paths' bug.
issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR v2 spec: columns at forEach level should resolve against the parent resource context
issues.evidence: ViewDefinition with forEach='name' on Patient, column path='id' returns NULL for all rows. SQL shows: fhirpath_text(name_elem_0, 'id') - the 'id' path is resolved against the name element, not the parent resource. Correct would be: fhirpath_text(t.resource, 'id').
issues.proposed_fix: Columns at forEach level that are not part of the forEach element's structure should resolve against the parent resource variable, not the unnested child.

issues.title: load_bundle crashes with AttributeError on non-dict entry items

issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4 Bundle.entry.resource must be a valid FHIR resource (JSON object)
issues.evidence: load_bundle({'entry': ['not a dict']}) raises AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'
issues.proposed_fix: Validate that each bundle entry is a dict before calling .get() on it. Raise TypeError or skip invalid entries.

issues.title: ViewDefinition where clause with valid FHIRPath comparison produces no results
issues.description: Even when using the correct where format ([{'path': 'gender = "male"'}] or {'path': 'gender = "male"'}), the generated SQL using fhirpath_bool cannot handle comparison expressions with embedded quotes. The SQL parser truncates the FHIRPath expression at the first inner quote. This means where clauses with string comparisons are fundamentally broken.
issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR v2: where should support FHIRPath boolean expressions
issues.evidence: where=[{'path': "gender = 'male'"}] causes SQL syntax error due to quote handling. Even direct fhirpath_bool calls with comparison expressions fail: fhirpath_bool(resource, 'gender = ''male''') causes ParserException.
issues.proposed_fix: Properly escape quotes in FHIRPath expressions embedded in SQL, or use parameterized queries for FHIRPath expressions
