issues.evidence: register(con) -> {'fhirpath_cpp': False, 'cql_cpp': False}; register(con) -> {'fhirpath_cpp': False, 'cql_cpp': False} (no error)

issues.title: fhirpath(NULL, path) correctly returns NULL per SQL NULL semantics
issues.description: fhirpath(NULL, 'id') returns None, which is correct SQL NULL propagation behavior. This confirms QA-D8A-035. Per FHIRPath R2 §3.1 and SQL conventions, NULL input should produce NULL output.
issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath R2 §3.1 (null handling). SQL NULL semantics.
issues.evidence: fhirpath(NULL, 'id') -> (None,)
issues.resolution_notes: Confirms QA-D8A-035 - this is correct behavior.

issues.title: DuckDB connection errors properly propagated
issues.description: DuckDB connection state errors (closed connection) are properly propagated as ConnectionException with clear message 'Connection already closed!'
issues.evidence: con.close(); loader.load_resources([resource]) -> ConnectionException: Connection already closed!

issues.title: ViewDefinition correctly detects duplicate column names per SQL-on-FHIR v2 spec
issues.description: The ViewDefinition parser correctly detects and reports duplicate column names with ValidationError, including the exact locations of duplicates. Per SQL-on-FHIR v2 spec, column names must be unique.
issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR v2: Column names must be unique within a ViewDefinition
issues.evidence: ValidationError: Duplicate column names across select tree: ['col1']. Column names must be unique per the SQL-on-FHIR v2 specification. (duplicate_names=['col1'], locations={'col1': ['select[0].column[0]', 'select[0].column[1]']})

issues.title: fhirpath_bool() returns None instead of False for boolean expressions
issues.description: fhirpath_bool() with a valid resource and 'gender = female' expression returns None instead of True or False. This may be due to how the boolean evaluation is handled, but it should return a boolean value for valid boolean FHIRPath expressions.
issues.evidence: fhirpath_bool({resourceType: Patient, gender: female}, 'gender = female') -> (None,)
issues.proposed_fix: Investigate why fhirpath_bool returns None for valid boolean expressions.

issues.title: ViewDefinition where clause passes through arbitrary FHIRPath including potential injection
issues.description: The where clause in ViewDefinition accepts arbitrary strings and passes them to fhirpath_bool() without validation. While FHIRPath expressions are safely handled (not SQL-executed), there is no validation that the where expression is valid FHIRPath before generating SQL. The SQL injection attempt '; DROP TABLE resources;--' is safely handled through FHIRPath parameterization.
issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR v2: Where clause should be valid FHIRPath
issues.evidence: where: ["'; DROP TABLE resources;--"] -> generates SQL with fhirpath_bool(t.resource, '\'; DROP TABLE resources;--') - safely parameterized
issues.proposed_fix: Consider validating where clauses as valid FHIRPath expressions during ViewDefinition parsing.

issues.title: CQL translator accepts nonexistent FHIR resource types in retrieve expressions
issues.description: When CQL code references a nonexistent FHIR resource type (e.g., [NonexistentResource]), the translator silently accepts it and generates SQL referencing the nonexistent type. Per CQL R1.5 §5, retrieve expressions should validate against the FHIR model. The ViewDefinition parser correctly warns about unrecognized resource types, but the CQL translator does not.
issues.spec_citation: CQL R1.5 §5: Retrieve expressions should validate against the FHIR model
issues.evidence: translate_cql('define Test: exists([NonexistentResource])') -> generates SQL with 'NonexistentResource' identifier, no error
issues.proposed_fix: Add validation of FHIR resource types in CQL retrieve expressions.

issues.title: ViewDefinition accepts missing name field without error
issues.description: generate_view_sql() accepts a ViewDefinition without a name field and generates SQL. Per SQL-on-FHIR v2 spec, name is a required field for ViewDefinitions. However, for SQL generation the name may not be strictly required.
issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR v2: name is a required field in ViewDefinition
issues.evidence: generate_view_sql({resource: Patient, select: [...]}) -> generates SQL without error (no name field)
issues.proposed_fix: Consider making name required in parse_view_definition().

issues.title: ViewDefinition with empty column array generates 'SELECT NULL WHERE FALSE'
issues.description: When a ViewDefinition has a select element with an empty column array (select: [{column: []}]), the function generates 'SELECT NULL WHERE FALSE' which is technically valid SQL but semantically meaningless. The parser validates that select array is non-empty but not that each select element has at least one column or nested select.
issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR v2: Each select element should have at least one column or nested select
issues.evidence: generate_view_sql({resource: Patient, select: [{column: []}]}) -> 'SELECT NULL WHERE FALSE'
issues.proposed_fix: Validate that each select element has at least one column or nested select with foreach.

issues.title: translate_library_to_sql() crashes with AttributeError when given CQL string
issues.description: translate_library_to_sql() raises AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'valuesets' when called with a CQL string. The function apparently expects a parsed library object, not a raw CQL string. The API should either accept strings or raise a clear TypeError.
issues.evidence: translate_library_to_sql(cql_string) -> AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'valuesets'
issues.proposed_fix: Add input type validation or document that the function requires a parsed library object.

issues.title: register_cql returns inconsistent values (None, True, False)
issues.description: When CQL UDFs are already registered, register_cql returns None instead of True/False. When first registering, it returns False (Python fallback). The return type should be consistent.
issues.evidence: First call: register_cql(con) -> False. Second call: register_cql(con) -> None
issues.proposed_fix: Make register_cql return consistent boolean values.

issues.title: attach/detach correctly validate SourceAdapter protocol
issues.description: fhir4ds.attach() and detach() correctly validate that the adapter argument implements the SourceAdapter protocol. They raise TypeError with clear messages: 'Expected a SourceAdapter, got NoneType. Ensure your adapter implements register() and unregister()'.
issues.evidence: attach(con, None) -> TypeError; attach(con, 'str') -> TypeError; detach(con, FakeAdapter()) -> TypeError

issues.title: fhirpath() processes non-FHIR JSON objects without warning
issues.description: When fhirpath() receives valid JSON that is not a FHIR resource (no resourceType field), it still processes FHIRPath expressions on it. For example, fhirpath('{"foo":1}', 'foo') returns ['1']. Per FHIR R4 §2.1, FHIR resources MUST have a resourceType. The FHIRPath engine should warn or error when processing non-FHIR JSON through the fhirpath() function.
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4 §2.1: Resources MUST have a resourceType element
issues.evidence: fhirpath('{"foo":1}', 'foo') -> (['1'],) - processes non-FHIR JSON without warning
issues.proposed_fix: Consider validating resourceType presence or adding a warning for non-FHIR JSON input.

issues.title: ViewDefinition source_table parameter enables SQL injection
issues.description: generate_view_sql() directly interpolates the source_table parameter into generated SQL without sanitization. An attacker-controlled source_table value like 'resources; DROP TABLE patients' produces multi-statement SQL with arbitrary DDL/DML. This is a textbook SQL injection vulnerability.
issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR v2 spec: ViewDefinition implementations must sanitize all external inputs. OWASP A03:2021 - Injection. generate_view_sql() API contract should validate source_table is a safe SQL identifier.
issues.evidence: generate_view_sql(vd, source_table='resources; DROP TABLE patients') generates: 'FROM resources; DROP TABLE patients t WHERE ...'. The semicolon allows arbitrary SQL injection. Similarly, source_table='' generates 'FROM  t' which is invalid SQL. Tested with: fhir4ds.generate_view_sql(vd_json, source_table='resources; DROP TABLE patients')
issues.proposed_fix: Validate source_table against SQL identifier regex: must match ^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$. Reject values containing semicolons, quotes, or other SQL metacharacters.

issues.title: ViewDefinition column path enables SQL injection into generated SQL
issues.description: generate_view_sql() embeds column paths directly into fhirpath_text() calls in generated SQL. A crafted path like "id') as \"id\" FROM resources; DROP TABLE resources; --" produces multi-statement SQL with DDL commands. While DuckDB's fhirpath_text() validates the expression at execution time, the generated SQL itself is malicious.
issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR v2 spec: Column paths must be valid FHIRPath expressions. The SQL generator should validate paths are syntactically valid FHIRPath before embedding in SQL.
issues.evidence: Column path 'id\') as \"id\" FROM resources; DROP TABLE resources; --' produces SQL: "fhirpath_text(t.resource, 'id'') as \"id\" FROM resources; DROP TABLE resources; --')". Generated SQL contains 'DROP TABLE' which is a DDL command. The SQL fails at execution because fhirpath_text validates the expression, but the generated SQL is still dangerous.
issues.proposed_fix: Validate column paths by attempting FHIRPath parse before SQL generation. Reject paths containing SQL metacharacters (quotes, semicolons) that could escape the fhirpath_text() call.

issues.title: ViewDefinition where clause embeds arbitrary strings in SQL
issues.description: generate_view_sql() embeds where clause FHIRPath expressions in fhirpath_bool() calls. A crafted where expression like "true') = true UNION SELECT secret FROM sensitive_data --" produces SQL with UNION injection. The where expressions are not validated as FHIRPath.
issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR v2 spec: where clauses must be valid FHIRPath expressions that evaluate to boolean. The generator should validate where expressions are parseable FHIRPath.
issues.evidence: where: ["gender = 'male'') OR (''1'' = ''1'"] produces SQL: "fhirpath_bool(t.resource, 'gender = ''male'') OR (''1'' = ''1') = true". The injected expression breaks out of the fhirpath_bool() call.
issues.proposed_fix: Validate where clause expressions by parsing them as FHIRPath before SQL generation.

issues.title: ViewDefinition forEach path enables SQL injection via alias generation
issues.description: generate_view_sql() uses forEach paths to generate SQL aliases. The path is sanitized for alias names (special chars replaced with underscores), but the raw path is still embedded in the fhirpath() call in generated SQL. Path 'name; DROP TABLE resources; --' produces SQL containing 'DROP TABLE'.
issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR v2 spec: forEach paths must be valid FHIRPath expressions.
issues.evidence: forEach: 'name; DROP TABLE resources; --' produces SQL containing: fhirpath(t.resource, 'name; DROP TABLE resources; --'). The alias is sanitized (name__DROP_TABLE_resources_____elem_0) but the raw path in fhirpath() is not.
issues.proposed_fix: Validate forEach/forEachOrNull paths as valid FHIRPath expressions before SQL generation.

issues.title: ViewDefinition repeat path enables SQL injection
issues.description: Similar to forEach, the repeat path is embedded in fhirpath_repeat() in generated SQL without validation. Path 'name; DROP TABLE resources; --' produces SQL containing 'DROP TABLE'.
issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR v2 spec: repeat paths must be valid FHIRPath expressions.
issues.evidence: repeat: ['name; DROP TABLE resources; --'] produces SQL: fhirpath_repeat(t.resource, '["name; DROP TABLE resources; --"]')
issues.proposed_fix: Validate repeat paths as valid FHIRPath expressions before SQL generation.

issues.title: FHIRPath evaluate() silently returns [] for non-dict resources (string, int, bool, None)
issues.description: evaluate(None, 'id'), evaluate('string', 'id'), evaluate(42, 'id'), evaluate(True, 'id') all silently return [] instead of raising TypeError. This is related to D8A-040/D8B-001 (silent [] for invalid JSON) but extends to non-dict Python types as well.
issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath spec: evaluate() expects a FHIR resource (dict/object). Non-dict inputs should raise TypeError.
issues.evidence: evaluate(None, 'id') -> []. evaluate('string', 'id') -> []. evaluate(42, 'id') -> []. evaluate(True, 'id') -> []. evaluate([], 'id') -> []. All silently return empty list.
issues.proposed_fix: Add type check at the start of evaluate(): if not isinstance(resource, (dict, list)): raise TypeError(...).

issues.title: DuckDB fhirpath() UDF returns [] for all invalid JSON inputs
issues.description: The fhirpath() DuckDB UDF returns [] (empty array) for any invalid JSON input including 'not json', '{broken', '', 'null', '42', '"str"', '[]'. It should either return NULL or raise an error for invalid JSON.
issues.spec_citation: DuckDB UDFs should have consistent NULL/error handling. Returning [] for invalid input conflates 'valid empty result' with 'invalid input'.
issues.evidence: SELECT fhirpath('not json', 'id') -> []. SELECT fhirpath('{broken', 'id') -> []. SELECT fhirpath('', 'id') -> []. All invalid JSON returns []. Meanwhile fhirpath(NULL, 'id') correctly returns NULL.
issues.proposed_fix: Return NULL for invalid JSON input, or raise an error. Never return [] for invalid input.

issues.title: CQL translator generates SQL with nonexistent resource types that produce wrong results
issues.description: CQL parse_cql('[FakeResource]') succeeds and the translator generates SQL containing 'FakeResource' as a resource type filter. When executed, the query returns results (the SQL doesn't fail) but the results are incorrect because FakeResource doesn't exist.
issues.spec_citation: CQL spec: Retrieve expressions must reference valid FHIR resource types. Translator should validate resource types against the FHIR specification.
issues.evidence: CQL: 'define InIP: exists [FakeResource]' -> parse_cql() succeeds -> translator generates SQL with 'FakeResource' -> SQL executes successfully but returns wrong results. Tested: FakeResource appears in generated SQL. Execute returns [('test-patient', False)].
issues.proposed_fix: Validate resource types in the CQL translator against known FHIR R4 types. Raise SemanticError for unknown resource types.

issues.title: FHIRDataLoader stores NaN/Infinity values as non-standard JSON
issues.description: load_resource() uses json.dumps() which serializes NaN and Infinity as bare tokens (not valid JSON per RFC 8259). Resources stored with NaN/Infinity values produce stored JSON like '{"value": NaN}' which is not valid JSON and breaks JSON interoperability.
issues.spec_citation: RFC 8259 (JSON spec): Numeric values must not include NaN or Infinity. json.dumps(resource) uses allow_nan=True by default.
issues.evidence: loader.load_resource({'resourceType':'Patient','id':'nan','value':float('nan')}) stores: '{"resourceType":"Patient","id":"nan","value":NaN}'. This is not valid JSON per RFC 8259. Same for Infinity values.
issues.proposed_fix: Use json.dumps(resource, allow_nan=False) or convert NaN/Infinity to null before serialization. Alternatively, validate resource values before storage.

issues.title: CQLToSQLTranslator.translate_library_to_population_sql(None) raises unhelpful AttributeError
issues.description: Passing None or a string to translate_library_to_population_sql() raises 'AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'valuesets'' instead of a clear TypeError.
issues.spec_citation: API contracts should validate input types and raise TypeError with clear messages.
issues.evidence: translator.translate_library_to_population_sql(library=None) -> AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'valuesets'. translator.translate_library_to_population_sql(library='string') -> AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'valuesets'.
issues.proposed_fix: Add type validation at the start of translate_library_to_population_sql(): if not isinstance(library, Library): raise TypeError('Expected Library object, got ...')

issues.title: CQL parse_cql(None/int/float) raises unhelpful TypeError without mentioning 'string'
issues.description: parse_cql(None) raises 'TypeError: object of type 'NoneType' has no len()' which is a raw Python error that does not mention that a string was expected.
issues.spec_citation: API contracts should validate input types and provide clear error messages.
issues.evidence: parse_cql(None) -> TypeError: object of type 'NoneType' has no len(). parse_cql(42) -> TypeError: object of type 'int' has no len(). Error message should say 'Expected string, got NoneType'.
issues.proposed_fix: Add explicit type check: if not isinstance(cql_text, str): raise TypeError('Expected string, got ...')

issues.title: FHIRPath compile() silently succeeds on empty/whitespace/invalid expressions
issues.description: compile(''), compile('   '), and compile(')') all succeed without error. The compiled function then crashes with KeyError: 'children' when called. The error should occur at compile time.
issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath spec: Empty or whitespace-only expressions are not valid FHIRPath. compile() should validate the expression at compile time.
issues.evidence: fn = compile(''); fn({'id':'test'}) -> KeyError: 'children'. fn = compile('   '); fn({'id':'test'}) -> KeyError: 'children'. fn = compile(')'); fn({'id':'test'}) -> KeyError: 'children'. All succeed at compile time, fail at execution with internal error.
issues.proposed_fix: Validate parse result in compile(): check that parsed AST has expected structure. Raise FHIRPathSyntaxError for empty/whitespace expressions.

issues.title: FHIRDataLoader.load_valuesets() raises AttributeError for non-list inputs
issues.description: load_valuesets('string') raises AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'. load_valuesets([None]) raises AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'. These should be TypeError with clear messages.
issues.spec_citation: API contracts should validate input types.
issues.evidence: load_valuesets('string') -> AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'. load_valuesets([None]) -> AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'.
issues.proposed_fix: Add type validation: check valuesets is a list, check each element is a dict/object.

issues.title: FHIRPath evaluate() with options['userInvocationTable']='string' raises unhelpful AttributeError
issues.description: Passing userInvocationTable as a string in options causes AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'items' instead of a clear TypeError.
issues.spec_citation: Options validation should catch type mismatches early.
issues.evidence: evaluate({'id':'test'}, 'id', options={'userInvocationTable': 'string'}) -> AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'items'.
issues.proposed_fix: Validate options types: userInvocationTable must be dict.

issues.title: CQL parser silently accepts type mismatches (int + string, bool and int) without error
issues.description: The CQL parser accepts '1 + "hello"', 'true and 5', and other type mismatches without raising any error. These should be caught during semantic analysis.
issues.spec_citation: CQL spec: Type checking must occur during static analysis. Operations like int + string are type errors.
issues.evidence: parse_cql('define Test: 1 + \'hello\'') succeeds. parse_cql('define Test: true and 5') succeeds. parse_cql('define Test: NonexistentFunction()') succeeds. All produce SQL that will give wrong results at runtime.
issues.proposed_fix: Add type checking to the CQL semantic analysis phase.

issues.title: FHIRPath evaluate() returns Decimal('Infinity')/Decimal('NaN') which are not JSON-serializable
issues.description: When evaluating FHIRPath on a resource containing float('inf') or float('nan'), the result includes Decimal('Infinity') or Decimal('NaN') which cannot be serialized with json.dumps().
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4: Decimal values should be valid JSON numbers. NaN/Infinity are not valid JSON.
issues.evidence: evaluate({'value': float('inf')}, 'value') -> [Decimal('Infinity')]. json.dumps([Decimal('Infinity')]) -> TypeError: Object of type Decimal is not JSON serializable.
issues.proposed_fix: Convert Decimal Infinity/NaN to None or string representation in the result.

issues.title: CQLToSQLTranslator accepts None connection and generates SQL without validation
issues.description: CQLToSQLTranslator(connection=None) succeeds, and translate_library_to_population_sql() generates SQL without any database connection. This is misleading - the SQL may not be valid for the target database but the user has no indication.
issues.spec_citation: API contracts: constructor should validate required parameters.
issues.evidence: CQLToSQLTranslator(connection=None) -> succeeds. translator.translate_library_to_population_sql(library) -> generates 712 chars of SQL. No error despite None connection.
issues.proposed_fix: Add validation: if connection is None and it's required, raise TypeError.

issues.title: FHIRPath evaluate({}) returns [] but evaluate({'id':'x'}) returns ['x'] without resourceType
issues.description: An empty dict returns [] but a dict with just 'id' returns the id value. The behavior is consistent (empty dict has no 'id' field) but may confuse users.
issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath spec: Resources should have a resourceType field.
issues.evidence: evaluate({}, 'id') -> []. evaluate({'id':'x'}, 'id') -> ['x'].
issues.proposed_fix: No fix needed - behavior is correct, just potentially surprising.

issues.title: generate_view_sql(source_table='') generates syntactically invalid SQL
issues.description: Passing source_table='' produces 'FROM  t WHERE ...' which is invalid SQL because the table name is empty. This should be caught during validation.
issues.spec_citation: generate_view_sql() should validate source_table is a non-empty string.
issues.evidence: generate_view_sql(vd, source_table='') -> 'FROM  t WHERE ...'. Executing this SQL: CatalogException: Table with name 't' does not exist.
issues.proposed_fix: Validate source_table is a non-empty valid SQL identifier.

issues.title: CQL parser accepts multiple context declarations without error
issues.description: parse_cql('context Patient\ncontext Population\ndefine Test: true') succeeds. The last context wins silently, which may not match user intent.
issues.spec_citation: CQL spec: Multiple context declarations are allowed but may be confusing.
issues.evidence: Two context declarations in same library parsed successfully.
issues.proposed_fix: Consider warning when context changes within a library.

issues.title: FHIRDataLoader.load_resource() accepts whitespace-only id without validation
issues.description: load_resource({'resourceType':'Patient','id':' '}) succeeds and stores the resource with a whitespace-only id. FHIR R4 specifies id must be a non-empty string matching [A-Za-z0-9\-\.]{1,64}.
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4: id must match regex [A-Za-z0-9\-\.]{1,64}. Whitespace-only id violates this.
issues.evidence: load_resource({'resourceType':'Patient','id':' '}) -> stored with id=' '.
issues.proposed_fix: Validate id against FHIR R4 id regex before storage.

issues.title: ViewDefinition where clause FHIRPath expression enables SQL injection via fhirpath_bool()
issues.description: The where clause expression is embedded in fhirpath_bool() SQL. A crafted expression like "gender = 'male'') OR (''1'' = ''1" produces SQL: fhirpath_bool(t.resource, 'gender = ''male'') OR (''1'' = ''1') = true. The single quotes in the FHIRPath expression are doubled (SQL escaping) but the expression structure allows breaking out of the fhirpath_bool() call.
issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR v2: Where expressions must be validated as valid FHIRPath boolean expressions.
issues.evidence: where: ["gender = 'male'') OR (''1'' = ''1"] generates: "AND fhirpath_bool(t.resource, 'gender = ''male'') OR (''1'' = ''1') = true". The OR breaks out of the fhirpath_bool() context.
issues.proposed_fix: Parse and validate where clause expressions as FHIRPath before SQL generation. Use parameterized queries for FHIRPath expressions instead of string embedding.

issues.title: CQL parser accepts SQL keywords (DROP, DELETE) as definition names
issues.description: parse_cql('define DROP: true') and parse_cql('define DELETE: true') both succeed. If these names appear in generated SQL, they could cause syntax errors.
issues.spec_citation: CQL spec: Identifiers should not conflict with SQL keywords in generated code.
issues.evidence: parse_cql('library L\nusing FHIR version \'4.0.1\'\ndefine DROP: true') -> succeeds.
issues.proposed_fix: Consider quoting generated SQL identifiers to prevent keyword conflicts.

issues.title: FHIRPath lexer exposes raw ANTLR4 LexerNoViableAltException with unhelpful messages
issues.description: Expressions with null bytes or high bytes produce 'LexerNoViableAltException('')' or 'LexerNoViableAltException(\xff\xfe)' with stderr message 'unknown recognition error type: LexerNoViableAltException'. These are internal ANTLR4 implementation details.
issues.spec_citation: Error messages should be user-friendly, not expose parser implementation details.
issues.evidence: evaluate(resource, '\x00id') -> LexerNoViableAltException('') with stderr: 'unknown recognition error type: LexerNoViableAltException'.
issues.proposed_fix: Catch ANTLR4 exceptions in the parser and convert to FHIRPathSyntaxError with user-friendly messages.

issues.title: FHIRPath evaluate('') raises KeyError: 'children' instead of proper error
issues.description: evaluate(resource, '') or evaluate(resource, '   ') produces no parse error, but then crashes with KeyError: 'children' when trying to access the parsed AST. This is an internal implementation error leaked to the user.
issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath spec: Empty expressions are not valid. Should raise FHIRPathSyntaxError.
issues.evidence: evaluate({'id':'test'}, '') -> KeyError: 'children'. The parse() function returns an empty parentStack which has no 'children' key.
issues.proposed_fix: Validate parse result: if AST is empty/invalid, raise FHIRPathSyntaxError('Empty FHIRPath expression').

issues.title: FHIRPath evaluate(')') and evaluate('(') raise KeyError instead of syntax error
issues.description: Single parentheses produce no parse error but crash with KeyError: 'children' when the code tries to access parsed AST children.
issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath spec: Invalid expressions should raise FHIRPathSyntaxError.
issues.evidence: evaluate({'id':'test'}, ')') -> KeyError: 'children'. evaluate({'id':'test'}, '(') -> KeyError: 'children'.
issues.proposed_fix: Validate parse result structure before accessing children.

issues.title: ViewDefinition resource type validation properly catches SQL injection attempts
issues.description: The parser validates resource types with a regex: ValidationError is raised for 'Patient\' UNION SELECT * FROM resources --'. This is correctly handled.
issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR v2: Resource types must be valid FHIR type names.
issues.evidence: generate_view_sql with resource='Patient\' UNION SELECT...' -> ValidationError: Invalid SQL identifier.
issues.proposed_fix: No fix needed - this is correctly handled.

issues.title: ViewDefinition column name validation properly catches SQL injection attempts
issues.description: The generator validates column names: ValidationError is raised for names containing semicolons, quotes, or other SQL metacharacters.
issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR v2: Column names must be valid SQL identifiers.
issues.evidence: generate_view_sql with name='col"; DROP TABLE...' -> ValidationError: Invalid SQL identifier.
issues.proposed_fix: No fix needed - this is correctly handled.

issues.title: CQL parser accepts duplicate define statements without warning
issues.description: parse_cql('define Test: true\ndefine Test: false') succeeds. The second definition silently overwrites the first.
issues.spec_citation: CQL spec: Duplicate definitions should produce a warning or error.
issues.evidence: Two 'define Test:' statements in same library parsed successfully.
issues.proposed_fix: Add warning or error for duplicate definition names.

issues.title: FHIRDataLoader.load_resources([valid, None, valid]) crashes with unhelpful error
issues.description: When load_resources() encounters a None element in the list, it crashes with AttributeError because None doesn't have a .get() method. This is after some resources may have already been processed.
issues.spec_citation: API should validate all elements before processing to ensure atomic behavior.
issues.evidence: load_resources([{'resourceType':'Patient','id':'p1'}, None, {'resourceType':'Patient','id':'p2'}]) -> crashes partway through processing. Some resources may be partially loaded.
issues.proposed_fix: Pre-validate all elements before any processing: check all items are dicts with resourceType.

issues.title: H1a: Duplicate resource ID handling - same id, different content
issues.description: When loading Patient(id=P1) then Patient(id=P1) with different data, does the loader deduplicate, overwrite, or create duplicates?
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4: Resources should be uniquely identified by resourceType + id
issues.evidence: Second load overwrote first (last-write-wins). Count=1. Gender=female. This is consistent but may lose data silently.
issues.proposed_fix: Loader should either deduplicate or raise an error when duplicate IDs are loaded

issues.title: H1b: Same ID across different resource types
issues.description: Patient(id='X') and Observation(id='X') - same id but different resourceType. FHIR allows this as identity is resourceType+id.
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4: Resource identity is the tuple (resourceType, id)
issues.evidence: OK: Both resources preserved correctly. Patient and Observation with same id='X1' coexist. Count=2.
issues.proposed_fix: Loader should handle resourceType+id as the composite key, not just id

issues.title: H1c: Bundle with duplicate resources
issues.description: A FHIR bundle contains two Patient resources with the same id but different content. How does load_bundle handle this?
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4 Bundles may contain duplicates; resolution strategy is implementation-defined
issues.evidence: Deduplicated to 1 resource. Kept gender=female. Bundle reported 1 loaded but only 1 stored.
issues.proposed_fix: Document behavior and/or provide deduplication option

issues.title: H1d: Clear and reload data integrity
issues.description: After clear(), verify that reloading produces correct data without phantom records.
issues.evidence: OK: Clear correctly removed all data and reload worked properly.

issues.title: H2a: Dangling subject reference - Observation references non-existent Patient
issues.description: Load Observation with subject=Patient/GHOST that doesn't exist. Does the loader validate references? Can queries still work? Do join-based queries produce empty results silently?
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4: References should be resolvable but servers are not required to enforce this
issues.evidence: Dangling reference accepted silently. Observation OBS-1 references Patient/GHOST which doesn't exist. LEFT JOIN returns NULL patient_id. Queries work but produce incomplete data.
issues.proposed_fix: Optionally validate referential integrity; at minimum document that dangling references are allowed

issues.title: H2b: Circular references between resources
issues.description: Patient references RelatedPerson which references back to the same Patient. Test if circular references cause infinite loops or errors.
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4: Circular references are valid but tools should handle them gracefully
issues.evidence: OK: Circular references handled gracefully. Patient links to RelatedPerson/RP-CIRC, RelatedPerson links to Patient/P-CIRC. No infinite loop.
issues.proposed_fix: Ensure queries do not infinitely recurse on circular references

issues.title: H2c: Self-referencing resource
issues.description: Patient with link pointing to itself. Test for infinite loops in self-referencing scenarios.
issues.evidence: OK: Self-referencing resource handled without issues. Link resolves to Patient/P-SELF.

issues.title: H2d: Condition without required subject field
issues.description: Load a Condition with no subject field. FHIR spec requires Condition.subject but bad data may be missing it.
issues.evidence: BUG: Condition without required subject field was accepted. FHIR spec requires Condition.subject (1..1 cardinality). Subject resolved to: (None,). Invalid data loaded without validation.
issues.proposed_fix: Loader should validate required fields and reject or warn about invalid resources

issues.title: H2e: Malformed resource references
issues.description: References with invalid formats: missing slash, empty string, UUID format, URL format.
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4 Reference can be relative (ResourceType/id), absolute URL, or UUID
issues.evidence: All malformed references accepted and stored verbatim. Total resources loaded: 5. No validation of reference format performed.
issues.proposed_fix: Document which reference formats are supported

issues.title: H3a: Invalid date formats in birthDate field
issues.description: Load Patients with invalid birthDate values (not-a-date, 2024-13-45, empty string, numeric). Do FHIRPath queries crash or silently return wrong results?
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4 date type must match YYYY-MM-DD format
issues.evidence: Invalid dates accepted without validation. All 5 resources loaded. FHIRPath operations on invalid dates may return unexpected results or None.
issues.proposed_fix: Validate date formats during load or return clear errors in FHIRPath evaluation

issues.title: H3b: Non-numeric valueQuantity.value
issues.description: Load Observation with valueQuantity.value='high' (string) instead of a number. Does FHIRPath numeric comparison crash or silently fail?
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4 Quantity.value is decimal (numeric) type
issues.evidence: String valueQuantity.value='high' loaded without error. FHIRPath may return None for numeric operations on non-numeric data, silently excluding records from clinical criteria.
issues.proposed_fix: Type coercion or validation of numeric fields; clear error on type mismatch in comparisons

issues.title: H3c: Mismatched code systems across resources
issues.description: Same clinical concept coded in different code systems (LOINC vs SNOMED) or same system with slightly different URLs. Queries using one system miss data from the other.
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4: Code systems are identified by URI; different URIs = different codes even if semantically equivalent
issues.evidence: 5 observations with same clinical code but different system URIs. Standard LOINC query matched 1/5 (20%). 4 observations silently missed due to code system URL variations.
issues.proposed_fix: Document that code system matching is exact. Provide terminology mapping guidance.

issues.title: H3d: Invalid or unknown resourceType
issues.description: Load a resource with resourceType='NotRealResource'. Does the loader accept it? Can it be queried?
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4: resourceType must be a valid FHIR resource name
issues.evidence: BUG: Unknown resourceType 'NotRealResource' accepted and stored. resourceType in DB: NotRealResource. No validation of resource type.
issues.proposed_fix: Validate resourceType against known FHIR resource types

issues.title: H3e: Missing resourceType field
issues.description: Load a resource dict with no resourceType key. This should always be rejected.
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4: resourceType is mandatory for all resources
issues.evidence: Exception: ValueError: Resource must have a 'resourceType' field. Got keys: ['gender', 'id']
issues.proposed_fix: Loader must reject resources without resourceType

issues.title: H3f: Empty or missing resource id
issues.description: Load resources with id='' or no id field at all. How does the system handle identity?
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4: id is 0..1 but when present must be non-empty string
issues.evidence: Resources with empty/missing ID were accepted. Total: 2. Rows: [('', 'Patient', 'male'), (None, 'Patient', 'female')]. Identity management is compromised.
issues.proposed_fix: Reject resources with empty id, generate UUID for missing id, or document behavior

issues.title: H4a: Future-dated clinical resources
issues.description: Load Conditions and Observations with dates far in the future (2099). Do date-based queries include or exclude these? Are they treated as valid clinical data?
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4: dateTime is a point in time; no constraint on future dates
issues.evidence: Future-dated Observation (2099) treated identically to valid dates. Query 'effectiveDateTime > @2024-01-01' returns both OBS-NORMAL (2024) and OBS-FUTURE (2099). 2/2 observations matched. Clinical reasoning may incorrectly include future data as if it were current.
issues.proposed_fix: Optionally flag or filter future-dated resources; document that temporal queries include future data

issues.title: H4b: Extreme past dates
issues.description: Load Patient with birthDate='1800-01-01' and '0001-01-01'. Test date arithmetic.
issues.evidence: Extreme past dates handled without crash. Date comparisons work but may produce semantically questionable results (e.g., patient born in year 0001).

issues.title: H4c: Overlapping period data in encounters
issues.description: Two Encounters for same patient with overlapping date ranges. Does the system handle this correctly?
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4: Period uses start/end dates; overlapping periods are allowed
issues.evidence: OK: Overlapping periods stored and queryable correctly. ENC-1 (Jan 1-10) and ENC-2 (Jan 5-15) coexist.

issues.title: H4d: Versioned resources via meta.versionId
issues.description: Load Patient with meta.versionId=1 then same id with meta.versionId=2. How does the system handle version tracking?
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4: meta.versionId tracks resource versions
issues.evidence: Last-write-wins: 1 row stored. versionId=2, gender=female. No version history preserved. Clinical reasoning only sees the latest version.
issues.proposed_fix: Document version handling behavior

issues.title: H4e: Period with end before start
issues.description: Load Encounter with period.start='2024-06-01' and period.end='2024-01-01' (end before start). Is this validated?
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4: period.end SHALL be greater than or equal to period.start
issues.evidence: BUG: Encounter with invalid period (end before start) accepted. start=2024-06-01T00:00:00Z, end=2024-01-01T00:00:00Z. FHIR spec requires period.end >= period.start. Duration calculations may return negative values.
issues.proposed_fix: Validate that period.end >= period.start during loading or querying

issues.title: H5a: Patient without birthDate - date query behavior
issues.description: Load Patient with no birthDate. Test FHIRPath date queries and comparisons.
issues.evidence: Missing birthDate returns None for date comparison (not crash). This is acceptable behavior - patients without birthDate are excluded from date-based filters.
issues.proposed_fix: FHIRPath date comparisons on missing fields should return empty/null, not crash

issues.title: H5b: Condition without clinicalStatus - active filter behavior
issues.description: Load Condition with no clinicalStatus. Test if 'active' filter misses it (should it be treated as active or excluded?).
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4: Condition.clinicalStatus is 0..1 in STU3 but required in many profiles
issues.evidence: Condition without clinicalStatus (COND-NOSTATUS) is EXCLUDED from 'active' filter. Only 1/2 conditions matched. Clinically, this condition may be active but is invisible to status-based queries.
issues.proposed_fix: Document how conditions without clinicalStatus are handled in active/resolved filters

issues.title: H5c: Observation without value - comparison behavior
issues.description: Load Observation with no valueQuantity. Test numeric comparison queries.
issues.evidence: Observation without value loaded successfully. fhirpath_number returns None for missing value. Comparison behavior needs testing with CQL queries.
issues.proposed_fix: Return None for missing value comparisons rather than crashing

issues.title: H5d: Empty coding array in CodeableConcept
issues.description: Observation with code.coding = [] (empty array). Test code-based queries.
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4: CodeableConcept.coding is 0..* but meaningful use requires at least one coding
issues.evidence: Observation with empty coding array loaded. Code filter (exists()) returned 1/2 results. Empty coding observation is excluded from code-based queries, which is expected but the resource should probably not have been loaded.
issues.proposed_fix: Return empty/null for queries on empty coding arrays

issues.title: H5e: ViewDefinition with null fields - output quality
issues.description: Generate ViewDefinition view and query it when some Patients have null birthDate. Does the view contain NULLs that could corrupt downstream analysis?
issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR v2: columns may be null if FHIRPath evaluates to empty
issues.evidence: ViewDefinition generated view with 3 NULL fields out of 12 total. Patients with missing data produce NULL columns. Rows: [('P-EMPTY', None, None), ('P-FULL', 'male', '1990-01-15'), ('P-NOBD', 'female', None), ('P-NOGENDER', None, '1985-03-20')]
issues.proposed_fix: Document nullability behavior in generated views

issues.title: H5f: Minimal resource with almost no fields
issues.description: Load Patient with only resourceType and id - no gender, no birthDate, no name. Test all FHIRPath queries.
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4: Many Patient fields are optional
issues.evidence: Minimal Patient (only resourceType + id) loaded and queryable. All optional fields return None/null. No crashes.

issues.title: H6a: Large dataset with systematic null fields
issues.description: Load 500 patients with 30% missing birthDate, 20% missing gender. Test aggregate queries for accuracy.
issues.evidence:
Exception: BinderException: Binder Error: Macro Substring() does not support the supplied arguments. You might need to add explicit type casts.
Candidate macros:
	Substring(s, start)

LINE 3:                 substring(fhirpath_text(resource, 'Patient.birthDate'),...
                        ^
issues.proposed_fix: Provide data quality profiling tools

issues.title: H6b: Mixed valid/invalid resources in batch load
issues.description: Load 10 resources where some are invalid (missing resourceType, malformed JSON). Does the entire batch fail or do valid resources get loaded?
issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4: Batch processing should handle individual failures gracefully
issues.evidence: All-or-nothing: 0 resources loaded after batch with invalid entries. Entire batch failed due to invalid resources.
issues.proposed_fix: load_resources should catch individual resource errors and continue with valid ones, reporting partial failures

issues.title: H6c: Large dataset ViewDefinition query performance
issues.description: Load 1000 patients with mixed data quality and measure ViewDefinition query time.
issues.evidence: OK: 1000 patients loaded in 0.70s. View query in 0.028s. Aggregation in 0.113s. Performance acceptable.

issues.title: H6d: Duplicate detection in large dataset
issues.description: Load 200 patients with 20 intentional duplicates. Test if we can detect duplicates via SQL queries.
issues.evidence: Loader deduplicates (last-write-wins). 200 resources attempted, 180 stored. 20 duplicates were silently overwritten. No way to detect that data was lost.
issues.proposed_fix: Provide duplicate detection query or utility

issues.title: CQL: AgeInYears with missing birthDate
issues.description: CQL library using AgeInYears() evaluated against patients with and without birthDate. Does it crash, skip, or return null?
issues.spec_citation: CQL spec: AgeInYears() returns Integer from Patient.birthDate
issues.evidence:
CQL evaluate_measure failed: BinderException: Binder Error: No function matches the given name and argument types 'YearsBetween(VARCHAR, DATE)'. You might need to add explicit type casts.
	Candidate functions:
	YearsBetween(VARCHAR, VARCHAR) -> BIGINT


LINE 8: SELECT _pt.patient_id, YearsBetween((SELECT _pd.birth_date FROM _patient_demographic
issues.proposed_fix: CQL should handle missing birthDate gracefully, returning null for AgeInYears()

issues.title: CQL: Observation value comparison with null values
issues.description: CQL query filtering Observations by value > threshold, where some observations have no value.
issues.spec_citation: CQL spec: null comparisons should return null (three-valued logic)
issues.evidence:
CQL value comparison with nulls:   patient_id                  HighBP
0         P1  [Observation/OBS-HIGH]

issues.title: CQL: Measure evaluation on empty database
issues.description: Evaluate a CQL measure against an empty database (no resources at all). Should return 0 counts, not crash.
issues.spec_citation: CQL spec: empty collections should be handled gracefully

issues.description: Navigate FHIRPath expressions through missing intermediate elements, e.g., Observation.referenceRange.low.value when referenceRange doesn't exist.
issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath spec: navigation through missing elements returns empty collection
issues.evidence: FHIRPath navigation through missing intermediate elements returns None consistently. No crashes on deep null navigation.

issues.title: JSON data integrity after load/query cycle
issues.description: Load complex FHIR resources and verify that extracting the full resource JSON returns identical data.
issues.evidence: OK: Complex JSON resource preserved perfectly through load/query cycle.

issues.title: audit_mode parameter is completely ignored in cql.evaluate_measure()
issues.description: The audit_mode parameter ("none", "population", "full") is accepted by evaluate_measure() but is never actually used. In fhir4ds/cql/__init__.py, the audit_mode parameter is declared in the function signature but never passed to CQLToSQLTranslator or translate_library_to_population_sql(). The translator has audit_mode/audit_expressions parameters in its __init__, but evaluate_measure never enables them. This means the entire audit functionality is a no-op: all 16 invalid audit_mode values (None, integers, booleans, lists, etc.) were silently accepted because the value is simply discarded. Valid audit modes produce identical output to audit_mode="none".
issues.spec_citation: CQL Measure Evaluation spec requires audit/evidence tracking for population criteria.
issues.evidence: In fhir4ds/cql/__init__.py evaluate_measure(): audit_mode is declared as parameter on line 8 but never referenced in the function body (lines 100-169). The translator is created as CQLToSQLTranslator(connection=conn) without audit_mode. CQLToSQLTranslator.__init__ supports audit_mode=True/False parameter. Result: audit_mode="none" and audit_mode="full" produce identical SQL and identical result DataFrames.
issues.proposed_fix: Pass audit_mode to CQLToSQLTranslator: translator = CQLToSQLTranslator(connection=conn, audit_mode=(audit_mode in ("population", "full")), audit_expressions=(audit_mode == "full")). Also validate audit_mode parameter values.

issues.title: Misleading error message when in_valueset UDF is missing
issues.description: When CQL uses URL-based ValueSet references in retrieve (e.g., [Observation: code in "http://..."]), the generated SQL uses in_valueset() UDF. If this UDF is not registered, DuckDB raises CatalogException. The evaluate_measure function catches this exception and re-raises it as ValueError with message "No FHIR data loaded" if the string contains "resources". But the real error is a missing UDF, not a missing table. This makes debugging very difficult.
issues.evidence: CatalogException: Scalar Function with name in_valueset does not exist! -> Caught and re-raised as: ValueError: No FHIR data loaded. The generated SQL references the resources table which does not exist. The CatalogException message contains no reference to "resources" but the error handler checks if "resources" is in the exception string (which it is, since the SQL query references the resources table).
issues.proposed_fix: Improve error detection: check if the CatalogException is about a missing table vs a missing function. Only show "No FHIR data loaded" when the error specifically refers to the resources table not existing.
